claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance during high-temperature exposure.
A thin, dense Al2O3 coating can be deposited on cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by PVD or an equivalent low-temperature method.
Using a low-temperature coating process will minimize alteration of the alloy's inherent microstructure.
The coating will form a continuous, adherent alumina layer on the alloy surface.
The continuous alumina layer will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The alumina diffusion barrier will prevent deleterious oxidation of the underlying HfNbTaTiZr.
The alumina coating will leave the bulk microstructure and intrinsic mechanical strength intact.
At 1000 °C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere, the coated alloy will exhibit significantly less oxygen uptake than the uncoated alloy.
At 1000 °C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere, the coated alloy will exhibit significantly less oxidation than the uncoated alloy.
After 100 hours of high-temperature oxygen exposure, the coated alloy will retain yield strength similar to the untreated baseline.
After 100 hours of high-temperature oxygen exposure, the coated alloy will retain ductility similar to the untreated baseline.
The proposed intervention does not alter the alloy's bulk composition or bulk processing route.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify cyclic tensile loading during evaluation in the oxygen-containing atmosphere, whereas the experiment describes a 100-hour exposure followed by tensile testing and does not specify cyclic loading. These represent materially different oxidation–mechanical coupling protocols.
